No test writes the real ~/.benchbox: integration CLI helpers run with an isolated HOME (show the diff); `ls -la ~/.benchbox/submission_salt` mtime unchanged after the full targeted test run.

description:
PROBLEM. Every path that publishes result identifiers refuses unless the operator sets BENCHBOX_MACHINE_ID_SALT (benchbox/core/results/anonymization.py:197-211); nothing generates or stores a salt. First-time submitters hit a refusal, agents repeatedly treated the salt as an owner blocker, and `benchbox export` / `benchbox publish run` silently anonymize with an EMPTY salt (exporter.py:99-103, publish.py:339), which the history-retention ADR amendment (2026-08-05) names a confirmation oracle.

PLAN (local plan reviewed adversarially; full text in context). Resolution order: explicit argument > BENCHBOX_MACHINE_ID_SALT (override) > existing salt file ~/.benchbox/submission_salt > generate (only on user-publication paths).
1. Store: ~/.benchbox/submission_salt (the name the owner's machine already uses). Generate `secrets.token_hex(32)`; create race-safe: temp file in the same dir, best-effort chmod 0600 (pattern: benchbox/security/credentials.py:72-75), fsync, `os.link` to the final path (FileExistsError -> read winner); on any other OSError (no hard links: SMB/FAT/FUSE) fall back to O_CREAT|O_EXCL. An empty winner file is re-read a bounded number of times, then raises telling the user to delete it. Never regenerate over an existing file. Parent dir created 0700 if absent. No new path env var; HOME controls location.
2. API (additive, no rename, public names in __all__ anonymization.py:812-823 stay): `resolve_public_pseudonym_salt` unchanged (env-only, soft, never raises); `require_public_pseudonym_salt` = explicit/env, then existing file, else MissingPublicPseudonymSaltError naming the file path and override; new `ensure_public_pseudonym_salt() -> tuple[str, bool]` (value, created). `AnonymizationConfig.machine_id_salt` becomes `field(default=None, repr=False)`. Retarget the error link to https://benchbox.dev/docs/contributing-results.html.
3. Callers that GENERATE (user publication): `benchbox submit` (resolve AFTER classification and refusals, not at submit.py:731; `--dry-run` never creates the file, previews with an in-memory salt and states where the file would be created; prints a one-line notice on creation naming the path, never the value), `benchbox export` (export.py:102-106), `benchbox publish run` (publish.py:339).
4. Callers that NEVER generate (corpus identity: the salt feeds the permanent result_id, transformer.py:1634-1635): scripts/stage_seed_corpus_bundle.py and _project/scripts/results_explorer_corpus_migrate.py use `require_` (env, then existing file, else refuse). The seed-corpus workflow keeps passing the secret; a missing secret still fails closed because runners have no salt file. No --require-env-salt flag.
5. Callers UNCHANGED (soft, env-only, must never raise): run capture (result_capture.py:1538), compare.py:1225, mcp/tools/benchmark.py:251, analytics.py:286, ResultExporter library default. Explorer pipeline (pipeline.py:564), CPU backfill and sync-results-data-to-published.yml keep `AnonymizationManager()` and read neither env nor file.
6. Tests: isolate HOME for integration CLI subprocess helpers (tests/integration/_cli_e2e_utils.py:23 and any other subprocess helper inheriting the real environment) so no test touches the real ~/.benchbox.
7. Docs in this repo: results-data/README.md salt section (automatic default, override, CI secret, backup, rotation changes result_id of re-staged results, ephemeral HOME gives a new salt per container); amendment to docs/internal/adr/adr-published-results-history-retention.md recording that a generated per-install private salt now meets the non-empty-salt requirement by default and supersedes the keep-empty decision (#1585), including the per-install vs cross-submitter trade-off and the storage location; changelog.d fragment (feat). User/API docs live in benchbox-site and are handled by site-docs-automatic-pseudonym-salt.
